parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime pairs a hostile national framework with a 'worst laws' state. Universal, traveler-facing exposures are documented: birth-sex passport/marker rules with reports of confiscated passports and stranding, a visa-refusal cable with a lifetime fraud ineligibility lever for suspected 'misrepresentation of sex,' national bans on identity-congruent access to government-funded single-sex facilities, and documented custodial abuse (forced labour, sexual abuse, hormone withdrawal) in national and immigration custody. The state adds a birth-sex school facility statute, a minor care ban, name-change denial for a trans teen, no gender-identity hate-crime statute, and a religious-refusal statute; a travelling parent with a trans minor faces direct exposure. Mitigants — marriage recognition, a national hate-crime statute with a 49-year federal murder sentence, near-background trans-specific violence (6.6 vs 6.0/100k), ~67% local support for anti-discrimination law, municipal protections, and active litigation — do not offset the unremedied entry and custody exposures. Elevated-to-high risk: 0.35.

entry_documents.exposure: Documented: passports issue only as birth-sex M/F; X markers discontinued; travellers report confiscation/blocks and stranding; visa cable directs refusal where sex is doubted and flags lifetime fraud ineligibility for suspected misrepresentation — universal exposure at every crossing.
entry_documents.protection: Ongoing national litigation against the passport policy; existing X passports valid until expiry; legal-aid FAQ guidance.
entry_documents.interaction: Document doubt at entry can escalate into visa refusal, fraud findings, or detention; state rules cannot displace the national screen.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: national corrections bureau mandates conversion-style policies (hair, hormone removal, psychiatric drugging); immigration custody forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men; prison reporting ceased.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Rescinded national prison EO not restored; no documented working remedy.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any arrest or visa detention routes a visitor into these national custody regimes; state jail placement (24-hour men's ward in the 2025 arrest) compounds it.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Documented: national bar on identity-congruent use of government-funded single-sex facilities; state statute mandates birth-sex bathrooms in public schools; 4 states criminalise facility use in circumstances, with a first arrest (handcuffed, men's ward) documented in one state; state defines sex by birth.
federal_state_facilities.protection: None documented; complaint in an analogous anchor-style rule confirmed exclusion. Not documented: adult enforcement of the state school rule.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A visiting parent accompanying a child in school-adjacent or state public buildings faces the state rule; national rule reaches federal buildings everywhere.

care_services.exposure: Documented: state ban on gender-affirming care under 18; national insurance bar proposed for minors; national care-order framed as 'mutilation'; state's main adolescent clinic closed. For an adult traveller, care access is not restricted.
care_services.protection: National employment-discrimination ruling (climate only); not a care protection.
care_services.interaction: A travelling trans minor loses care continuity in-state; a parent facilitating transition could face exposure under national school/teacher directives.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Documented: state supreme court calls a trans boy 'minor female'; state legal-risk tier 'legislatively erased transgender people'; religious-refusal statute gives service providers a refusal basis; national counterterrorism strategy targets 'radically pro-transgender' groups; 190+ anti-trans bills in one session.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; a federal 49-year sentence was imposed for a bias murder in this state.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State refusal statute and absent non-discrimination law leave visitors without service recourse; national prosecution remains the only bias-crime route.

minors_guardians.exposure: Documented: care ban under 18; name change denied for a consenting-parent trans teen; school sports and birth-sex bathrooms; teacher-prosecution directive; hospital record subpoenas for under-19 patients. A trans minor visitor is directly exposed; a guardian risks scrutiny.
minors_guardians.interaction: State and national orders interact: care, school and records all point to birth-sex treatment regardless of foreign or home documents.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Trans-specific killing rate 6.6/100k vs 6.0 general homicide — background-level, not a campaign; no state gender-identity bias statute; dress-code incident documented (resident student).
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal bias prosecution demonstrated; municipal protections in 4 cities; 2019/2024 polls show ~67% support for anti-discrimination law.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police lack bias-crime authority; recourse runs through national prosecutors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Uncertain: state facility-ban adult enforcement data absent; March 2026 licence law exceptions unknown; whether amended birth certificates carry dual markers on certified copies unknown; contested rulings unresolved; national measures partially enjoined, so operative exposure varies by travel date.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation and legal-aid resources; several orders blocked in court.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation could improve or worsen conditions; traveller exposure depends on measures in force at the moment of travel.

anchor_checks.comparison: Like 0.35-A, this jurisdiction has a documented universal facility rule and no working complaint remedy, but adds far heavier national entry-document and visa-fraud levers and documented custodial abuse — worse than 0.35-A on several axes, mitigated by near-background violence and some functioning protections.

0.45-D documents invasive unremedied screening as its worst feature; here entry exposure is broader (passport marker policy, visa fraud lever, stranding reports) and custody abuse is documented, pushing below that anchor despite milder street-level violence.

0.65-C pairs traditional acceptance with a dead-letter statute; here no comparable acceptance layer exists — the state is graded worst-in-class, the national posture is hostile, and only partial litigation relief operates, so the case cannot reach reduced risk.

0.25-D combines a birth-sex facility rule with police stops and extortion; this jurisdiction's facility scope (schools nationally, plus federal buildings) and documented custody harm are comparable, but its violence is near-background and some federal remedies exist — materially better than 0.25-D.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is national-first: every visitor passes through a border system that now issues only birth-sex markers, can refuse visas on doubted sex with a lifetime fraud lever, and has produced stranding reports; national custody, if entered, carries documented hormone withdrawal, forced labour and sexual abuse. The state adds its own hostile layer — birth-sex school facilities, a minors' care ban, name-change denial, no gender-identity protections, and a statutory refusal defence — placing it in the harshest graded tier. Countervailing evidence: trans-specific killing at roughly the general homicide rate, a federal bias-murder prosecution, marriage recognition, municipal ordinances, ~67% public support for anti-discrimination law, and ongoing litigation that has enjoined some measures. These soften the picture but do not neutralise the universal entry-document and facility exposures, which remain unremedied. The result is solidly elevated risk, at the lower edge of elevated for an adult alone and materially worse for an adult travelling with a trans minor.
